ranges.quote: There are tens of thousands of drivers moving around your city. Uber finds the closest one in about two hundred milliseconds. How?

ranges.quote: Here's the naive way. We calculate the distance from you to every single driver and sort. That's fine for fifty drivers, but it's a disaster for fifty thousand updating every second.
Instead, we index space itself. A quadtree splits the map into four squares, then splits the busy squares again, recursively.
ranges.reason: Single clean take, matches script verbatim.

ranges.quote: To find nearby drivers, we just walk down to your square and check its neighbors, ignoring the entire rest of the city. Geohashing does the same trick by turning coordinates into a short string, so nearby becomes a simple prefix match.

ranges.quote: Surge pricing and ETA come from ML models predicting demand on top of this geoindex. The index makes the lookup fast enough to feed the model in real time.
